chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: Her two trips to Britain and Ireland
summary: She played the London Casino in 1948 and a variety circuit in 1953-54, transposing arrangements for pit bands.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Okay. There are two things I guess most of all that you did before the retirement, two trips to Great Britain and Ireland.
And I guess you've talked about those.

Yeah, the first time I went over was in 1948, but I was still doing - oh, 'Loch Loman' got me there. I was supposed to go there in 1938 and then the war broke out and there was no exchange of artists between the two Continents and so I really didn't get there until 1948. But 'Loch Loman', when I got over there 'Loch Loman' wasn't the song that was the favorite over there. 'The Folks Who Live On The Hill' was the one that they had been playing on the hit parade for ten years. But the British Overseas Air Corporation, they sponsored for me to go to Loch Loman during my stay there. So I went up to see what it was all about. I thought Loch Loman was a hole in the ground. I had no idea it was the lake that it was. And so I spent a day up there at that time. And I was there during the Aurora Borealis. It never got dark all night. It was a strange experience.

So then when I came back I could say I had been there anyhow.
You played theaters on that tour?

I played the London Casino. I didn't play the Palladium. And I did some radio broadcasts while I was there. And I did a few theaters right in and around London. That's all I did the first time I was there. But I went back again in 1953 and I toured the Britist Isles I opened in London in a club.

I think that's the name of it, yeah. And I was there for eight weeks. And when I left there I went to Dublin and I played the Royal Theater there. And then I played Glasgow Dundee, and Aberdeen. Cardiff, I went to Wales and I came back to London and did a few theaters around London. And then I came home.
And you were accompanied by the pit band in each place?
You took your own arrangements with you?
That's right. That is when I

really got involved in transposing and fitting arrangements to fit the band. I guess I must have been over there about, oh about six months.
So you went at the end of '53?
I got there in the end of '53 and I was there through about April or May of '54 because I was in Dublin on St. Patrick's Day of 1954, March 17th. I had a good time. That's all I can say.
